course.title: Semantic search and AI knowledge bases
course.subtitle: Practical corporate course for applying AI to semantic search and knowledge bases, with exercises on realistic work, reusable materials and clear governance criteria.
course.summary: Practical corporate course for applying AI to semantic search and knowledge bases, with exercises on realistic work, reusable materials and clear governance criteria.
course.mode: In-person or online lab, with guided exercises and materials adapted to the client.
course.profileDescription: For technical teams with programming and software architecture basics.
course.problem: Companies often approach semantic search and knowledge bases through scattered experiments: a few prompts, a few enthusiastic users, many doubts about data, quality and responsibility. This course turns that uncertainty into an operating method. Participants work on realistic scenarios, learn where AI helps, where human review remains essential and how to make the practice repeatable inside the company.
course.audience: For technical teams with programming and software architecture basics.
course.whenToChoose: Choose this course when the company wants concrete progress on semantic search and knowledge bases and needs training that produces usable workflows, not abstract theory.
course.chooseIf: When the company wants concrete progress on semantic search and knowledge bases and needs training that produces usable workflows, not abstract theory.
outcomes: Map the work and the decisions where AI can reduce friction.
Build practical instructions, checklists and review criteria.

modules.title: Production and governance
modules.description: Monitoring, security, audit, cost and maintenance.

exercises: Map a realistic process connected to semantic search and knowledge bases.

materials: Operating canvas for semantic search and knowledge bases.
course.privacy: The course uses synthetic, public, anonymised or client-approved materials. It explains how to minimise data exposure, protect confidential information, verify outputs and keep human responsibility explicit.
course.prerequisites: Basic technical familiarity with software, data or system architecture is recommended.

faqs.question: Is the course tool-specific?
faqs.answer: No. Patterns and workflows are adapted to the tools and policies chosen with the client.

faqs.question: Can company data be used?
faqs.answer: Only when accounts, contracts and internal policies allow it. Otherwise synthetic or anonymised data is used.

faqs.question: What remains after the course?
faqs.answer: Reusable materials, examples, checklists and a clear set of next steps.

faqs.question: Is it theoretical?
faqs.answer: No. The course is built around practical exercises and decisions close to real work.

extraExamples.title: From generic training to the real process
extraExamples.description: A company asks for training on semantic search and knowledge bases, but the real issue emerges during mapping: repeated tasks, informal checks and distributed responsibilities. The path uses examples close to daily work and turns training into an initial operating model, not a theory session.

extraExamples.title: From individual experimentation to governed practice
extraExamples.description: Some people have already found shortcuts with AI while others are blocked. The course creates a shared base: what can be done, what must be reviewed, which data should not be exposed and when escalation is needed. The result is Operating canvas for semantic search and knowledge bases.

extraExamples.title: From enthusiasm to decision
extraExamples.description: Management needs to understand whether semantic search and knowledge bases deserves budget and continuity. The lab separates immediate benefits, operational risks and data dependencies. The company leaves with criteria for the next step instead of more isolated demos.

selectionCriteria: Choose this course if the main need concerns semantic search and knowledge bases, not a generic overview of AI.
Prefer it when there is a process, document, workflow or responsibility to work on during training.
Postpone it if there is no internal sponsor yet or if the issue is only buying a software licence.
Pair it with AI Workflow Redesign Lab when the company first needs to understand which processes deserve priority.
limits: It does not promise full automation or replacement of human responsibility.
It does not require confidential data to be uploaded into unapproved environments.
It is not legal, tax, HR or specialist technical advice when those responsibilities remain with competent functions.
It produces skills, criteria and reusable materials; continued adoption requires sponsorship, governance and internal practice.
